story_text.value:
I built Task629 to make the tracking of my personal development less time consuming. Instead of spending time thinking about how the tasks which I have completed fit into certain skills I am trying to develop, I pass this to a locally hosted AI.

As well as tracking individual skills which are demonstrated by tasks, there is functionality to work towards goals and to produce a report. This addition makes interview prep much simpler.

story_text.value:
I originally built ThemesFor.app in 2018 while running a small web development agency.

One thing that kept bothering me with website builders was that they increasingly tried to hide the technical parts of building a website. That's useful for many people, but I wanted almost the opposite — a visual tool for people who are already comfortable with HTML and CSS.

ThemesFor.app is my attempt at that.

You can build static websites from blocks, edit them visually, and export the HTML. I'm now working on taking the idea much further, but before I do, I wanted to put the current version in front of developers and see what they find useful—and what they don't.

It's still rough in places, so feedback is very welcome:

https://themesfor.app

title.value: Show HN: ThemesFor.app – a static website builder that doesn't hide the HTML

story_text.value:
Hi HN, I built GitGud out of frustration: no open-source Git GUI felt as nice as GitKraken. Bonus points if you get where the name comes from.

Highlights: undo for any git action (even rebases), drag a branch onto another to merge or rebase, interactive rebase and line-level staging.

It's open source, and feedback is really welcome!

title.value: Show HN: GitGud – a free, open-source Git GUI with undo for any action

story_text.value:
My friends and I have been toying with the idea of personalized (cycling indoor) training using AI to assist with planning and tailoring workouts around a busy schedule and ambitious goals, so I decided to build an experiment to see how it would work.

Cycling is a sport that's very hard on the body and many cyclists burn out or get frustrated when trying to improve, so my hypothesis is that with proper analysis of training data, there's a lot of potential to build a good product.

title.value: Show HN: I built an AI cycling coach
